title: An endpoint ledger for impressive demonstrations

sources.use: Separate task demonstrations from broad capability interpretation.
sources.boundary: A new frozen model cannot reproduce the unavailable early GPT-4 build.

sources.locator: Original hormone, risk and subjective endpoints; larger-sample replication and broader meta-analysis
sources.use: Transfer endpoint separation to AI evaluation.
sources.boundary: Neither effect sizes nor a verdict on posture transfer to AI.

mechanism: A fluent explanation, executable answer and successful transfer are different endpoints. Carry the endpoint distinctions emphasized by the power-posing dispute into a capability ledger so a persuasive narrative cannot substitute for correctness or robustness.
hypothesis: On a frozen local model, explanation fluency will show weaker agreement with held-out task correctness than executable checks do; an agreement gap below 0.10 would favor endpoint convergence over dissociation.
experiment: Preregister 60 procedurally generated logic/programming task families and four surface variants each. Freeze prompts, decoding and model checksum. Score exact solutions, executable tests, counterfactual transfer and a fixed textual-fluency rubric separately; bootstrap families, not variants.
baseline: Same 240 outputs, equal token budgets; compare an unweighted four-endpoint composite with the preregistered endpoint ledger. A generator provides hidden correct solutions. No evaluator sees task provenance.
metric: Family-level endpoint disagreement, correctness calibration, and the fluency-versus-executable agreement difference with bootstrap intervals.
falsifier: A narrow interval wholly below the 0.10 disagreement-gap threshold favors coherent endpoints; large preregistered dissociation favors reporting separate competencies.
confound: Rubric reliability and task difficulty can create apparent dissociation; retain raw scores and stratify by generator difficulty.
feasibility: Offline audit, 240 generations plus local tests; synthetic success does not establish general intelligence.

title: Cost denominators without a single understanding score

sources.use: Keep empirical resource accounting separate from conceptual and ethical claims.
sources.boundary: A local energy proxy cannot settle historical training emissions or social value.

sources.locator: Debt-bin aggregation; critical replication on weighting and inclusion; author response
sources.use: Audit how denominators and group weighting alter a summary.
sources.boundary: No debt threshold, causal direction or economics effect transfers.

mechanism: Different denominators answer different questions. Transfer the debt dispute's aggregation audit to AI resource evaluation: cost per request, cost per verified answer and cost per task family can rank the same systems differently without resolving ethical judgments.
hypothesis: Two frozen local models' cost rankings will reverse across at least two preregistered denominators if one gains accuracy mainly on long tasks; stable rankings would favor denominator robustness.
experiment: Use 80 synthetic task families, balanced easy/hard and short/long. Record wall time and generated tokens for one fixed attempt per model; use measured joules only if a supported meter exists. Report four denominators and all task failures.
baseline: Identical hardware, task families and output caps; alternate execution order. Compare equal-family weighting with request weighting. Treat tokens/time as proxies explicitly, never as emissions.
metric: Rank reversals, resource per verified answer, failure-inclusive totals and family-bootstrap intervals.
falsifier: Consistent rankings with narrow paired uncertainty across all four denominators weaken denominator sensitivity; reversals support a conditional efficiency conclusion.
confound: Warm-up, caching and output length; freeze cache policy, randomize order, and report uncached/cached strata.
feasibility: 160 local generations; a resource-accounting proposal only. The Parrots normative concerns remain separate even if efficiency improves.

title: Synthetic natural experiments for evidence use

sources.use: Turn selected task performance into a narrowly defined intervention test.
sources.boundary: No single benchmark identifies general intelligence or exactly repeats early GPT-4.

sources.locator: Original NJ/PA before-after comparison; 2000 comment and reply
sources.use: Transfer explicit comparison-group and measurement assumptions.
sources.boundary: A synthetic randomized intervention does not inherit wage-study effects or policy validity.

mechanism: An answer may follow supplied evidence or remembered associations. Transfer comparison-group scrutiny into a randomized synthetic evidence intervention: preserve task form while changing only a fictional rule, and compare changes against an untouched matched rule.
hypothesis: If answers use supplied rules, random rule reversals will shift the affected answers by at least 0.60 more than matched unaffected answers; generic prompt disruption predicts similar degradation in both.
experiment: Generate 100 fictional-world families with two independent rules and known answers. Randomly reverse one rule in half the families' paired prompts; retain unaltered companion questions. Freeze model, prompt template and scoring before collection.
baseline: Same families, token cap and query count for intervention and control. Estimate a paired difference in changes, with family as unit; include a neutral text-edit placebo of matched length.
metric: Difference-in-differences in rule-consistent answer probability, placebo degradation and family-randomization intervals.
falsifier: Near-zero targeted contrast with comparable affected/unaffected degradation favors disruption or shallow matching; a targeted contrast above 0.60 with low placebo effect favors evidence-sensitive behavior on these tasks.
confound: Rule ambiguity or changed tokenization; use balanced symbol assignments and deterministic ground-truth validation.
feasibility: Approximately 600 offline generations; intervention causality is confined to generated prompts and this frozen model.

title: Can anthropomorphic framing move judgments without performance?

sources.use: Separate interpretation of fluent outputs from measured behavior.
sources.boundary: A framing effect would not refute understanding or decide normative claims.

sources.locator: Original subjective, behavioral and physiological endpoint distinction; replication challenge
sources.boundary: No bodily-posture mechanism or empirical effect size transfers.

mechanism: Descriptions can influence evaluations without changing the underlying artifact. Transfer endpoint separation to an automated judge audit: manipulate anthropomorphic versus mechanical labels around identical outputs, while executable correctness remains fixed and separately recorded.
hypothesis: An automated judge susceptible to framing will change attributed-understanding scores by at least 0.5 on a seven-point scale across labels, while identical outputs retain identical correctness; a gap below 0.2 favors framing robustness.
experiment: Freeze 100 synthetic programming/logic outputs, balanced correct/incorrect by hidden tests. Present each output under randomized anthropomorphic, mechanical and neutral labels to a fixed local judge in isolated contexts; preregister rubric, order and thresholds.
baseline: Identical output bytes and equal judge-token budgets; correctness comes from the same executable tests, not judge agreement. Use artifact as the paired unit.
metric: Within-output label effect on understanding and correctness judgments, against invariant test results; report artifact-bootstrap intervals.
falsifier: A narrow effect interval within ±0.2 weakens the framing hypothesis. A >0.5 shift confined to interpretive ratings supports judgment sensitivity without proving anything about genuine understanding.
confound: Label text can leak intended ratings; use equal-length symmetric templates and include neutral-label repetition for stochastic variation.
feasibility: 300 automated judgments plus executable tests; evaluates a judge, not human susceptibility or ethical acceptability.

title: A replication passport for changing model builds

sources.use: Record which model, prompts and endpoints are actually reproducible.
sources.boundary: Unavailable early GPT-4 cannot be exactly replicated with a newer build.

sources.locator: Original nine experiments; Failing the Future retroactive-recall replications; 90-experiment follow-up
sources.boundary: Recall replication results do not adjudicate every Bem paradigm or any AI claim.

mechanism: A replication label can conceal a changed endpoint or system. Transfer paradigm matching from the Bem dispute into a machine-readable passport separating same-build reruns, template transfer and cross-build conceptual follow-ups before any AI result is compared.
hypothesis: For one frozen model, task-template transfer will reduce accuracy by at least 0.15 relative to same-template reruns if apparent reliability depends on presentation; a gap below 0.05 favors template robustness.
experiment: Preregister 80 synthetic task families, three equivalent templates and two fixed-seed runs. Archive model/tokenizer hashes, prompt bytes and all outcomes. Analyze same-build reproducibility and template transfer separately; any second model becomes a conceptual extension.
baseline: Same task families, decoding parameters and per-query token cap. Matched rerun and transfer contrasts use family averages, not individual prompts as independent observations.
metric: Exact-output repeatability, answer consistency and the template-transfer accuracy gap with family-bootstrap intervals.
falsifier: A narrow transfer gap under 0.05 weakens template dependence; a gap above 0.15 despite repeatable same-template outputs favors presentation-limited reliability.
confound: Equivalent templates might inadvertently differ in information; validate every template against a symbolic solver and archive rejected templates.
feasibility: 480 small local generations; no claimed reproduction of historical GPT-4 or of Bem's human experiments.

title: Replicate claim-specific audits, not whole-paper verdicts

sources.locator: Training-data curation, environmental costs and language-understanding sections
sources.use: Build separate empirical, conceptual and normative claim ledgers.
sources.boundary: A capability result cannot falsify the paper as a whole or settle its values.

sources.locator: Hormone/risk/self-report endpoints; larger replication; broader synthesis
sources.boundary: Later subjective-posture evidence is not a direct replication of every original endpoint.

mechanism: A whole-paper verdict conflates claims requiring different evidence. Transfer endpoint-specific replication bookkeeping to an AI argument audit, checking whether independently rerun extraction preserves the boundary between a measurable proposition, an interpretation and an ethical judgment.
hypothesis: A typed claim ledger will reduce invalid whole-paper refutation links by at least 30 percentage points versus an untyped summary when both process identical constructed evidence packets.
experiment: Construct 90 synthetic claim/evidence packets with author-written answer keys, balanced empirical/conceptual/normative and mixed-strength evidence. Freeze two extraction prompts; run isolated contexts twice. Include deliberately irrelevant capability successes and endpoint-mismatched follow-ups.
baseline: Equal packet counts, model, context and output-token budget; typed versus untyped extraction. Packet is the independent unit; exact keys encode scope relations rather than contested philosophical truth.
metric: Invalid-refutation rate, correct scope-link rate, omission rate and rerun agreement; paired packet-bootstrap intervals.
falsifier: A narrow improvement below 10 points or a compensating omission increase favors no useful ledger benefit; ≥30 points without omission inflation supports improved scope bookkeeping.
confound: Synthetic keys may privilege the ledger vocabulary; counterbalance wording and reserve paraphrased packet families before prompt design.
feasibility: 360 short local generations. This tests bookkeeping on constructed examples, not the truth of Parrots or power posing.

title: Task-family weighting versus the showcase average

sources.use: Make the sampling unit behind a broad capability summary explicit.
sources.boundary: Synthetic sampling cannot reconstruct undocumented historical selection decisions.

sources.locator: Country/year inclusion and weighting in original, critical replication and author response
sources.use: Transfer inclusion and aggregation sensitivity analysis.
sources.boundary: Corrected association does not establish a debt threshold, nor does weighting establish AI generality.

mechanism: Overrepresented easy families can dominate a pooled success rate. Transfer inclusion and weighting audits from historical economic summaries to AI demonstrations, retaining all generated tasks and showing exactly which family weights produce the reported capability headline.
hypothesis: A deliberately imbalanced showcase sample will overstate equal-family held-out accuracy by at least 0.15; balanced reporting should reduce that inflation below 0.05 when evaluated against the same known task population.
experiment: Preregister 12 synthetic task families, 20 instances each, and a sealed 10-per-family holdout. Freeze local model and scoring. Compare random showcases with an explicitly simulated curator selecting easy-family examples; audit all inclusions.
baseline: Equal showcase size and total generated-response budget. Compare pooled, equal-family and holdout-standardized estimates using the same outputs; never infer unobserved Sparks selection.
metric: Headline-minus-heldout accuracy, family coverage and worst-family accuracy; repeat sampling 1,000 times from the fixed output pool.
falsifier: Inflation below 0.05 even under specified imbalance favors robust aggregation; ≥0.15 inflation removed by balancing supports the proposed selection diagnostic.
confound: Task families may differ in semantic overlap, not only difficulty; publish generator definitions and stratify overlap using known construction labels.
feasibility: 360 local generations, then cheap resampling. Establishes an audit failure mode, not that the focal paper exhibits it.

title: A discovery-and-confirmation firewall for capability search

sources.use: Keep exploratory demonstrations distinct from locked confirmatory tests.
sources.boundary: Exploration is useful; this protocol makes no allegation about the authors' search history.

sources.locator: Original experimental set, retroactive-recall replications and 90-experiment meta-analysis
sources.use: Transfer prospective endpoint choice and selection sensitivity.
sources.boundary: No pooled effect or failed paradigm transfers to model competence.

mechanism: Trying many prompts can discover a useful interface and also select lucky outcomes. Transfer prospective replication discipline into a capability-search firewall: spend a fixed discovery budget, then lock the prompt and evaluate untouched task families with all attempts retained.
hypothesis: Selecting the best of 20 prompts on a small discovery set will produce a discovery-to-confirmation gap at least 0.10 larger than a preregistered fixed prompt under a matched total token budget.
experiment: Use 100 synthetic task families split before generation into discovery and sealed confirmation. Prespecify 20 wording variants. Allocate a fixed token budget to prompt search and confirmation; run 30 resampled family splits on a reusable fixed response matrix.
baseline: A fixed-prompt condition receives the identical overall response-token budget, with surplus spent on additional confirmation families; compare at equal total cost and report both equal-family subsets and expanded confirmation.
metric: Optimism gap, held-out correct families per million tokens, prompt-rank stability and family-level uncertainty.
falsifier: No excess optimism plus greater held-out correct families per token favors productive prompt discovery; a large gap with no budget-adjusted gain favors selection overfitting.
confound: Prompt search can be a legitimate part of the deployed system; define the evaluated system to include search and report its cost, not only the winning prompt.
feasibility: Up to 2,000 short offline generations with a hard token ceiling; simulation/resampling evaluates the protocol, not historical experiments.
